entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Aristobulus III of Judea (b. 52 BCE) was a Roman client king of Judea, a province of the Roman Empire, active in the Global region. He was a member of the Hasmonean dynasty and the last Hasmonean king. Known for his tumultuous relationships with Roman leaders and his attempts to maintain Judean independence.

Aristobulus III played a key role in the Jewish-Roman Wars, a series of conflicts that lasted from 66 BCE to 135 CE. He was a prominent figure in the Jewish resistance against Roman rule, using guerrilla warfare and diplomacy to fight against the Roman Empire's attempts to subjugate Judea.

Despite his efforts, Aristobulus III's reign was marked by instability and conflict. He was eventually defeated by the Roman general Pompey the Great's adopted son, Gnaeus Pompeius, in 35 BCE.

Aristobulus III's legacy is complex and multifaceted. His actions had significant consequences for the Jewish people and the Roman Empire, shaping the course of Jewish history and the Roman Empire's expansion into Judea.

The legacy of Aristobulus III is also marked by his involvement in the construction of the Temple in Jerusalem, one of the most sacred sites in Judaism. His efforts to maintain Judean independence and resist Roman rule had a lasting impact on the Jewish people and their connection to the Temple.

Aristobulus III's life and reign offer valuable insights into the complex dynamics of the Roman Empire and its interactions with the Jewish people. His story highlights the tensions and conflicts that arose between the Roman Empire and the Jewish people, shaping the course of Jewish history and the Roman Empire's expansion into Judea.
